questions.q: True or false? Our right back can mark both Blue attackers on that side alone.
questions.explain: Right, it's false. One defender cannot cover two runners, so our right winger recovers to help.
choiceExplanations: Two attackers against one defender is a 2v1. One quick pass beats our right back.
Right, it's false. One defender cannot cover two runners, so our right winger recovers to help.

questions.q: Put the lesson in order, from first to last.
options: Blue's right back joins the attack
Our right winger recovers with them
Our left winger tracks the new runner
questions.explain: Yes. A fourth runner joins, a winger tracks them, and the other winger does the same after the switch.
choiceExplanations: Yes. A fourth runner joins, a winger tracks them, and the other winger does the same after the switch.
Our right winger recovers only after Blue's right back starts the run.
Blue switches play after our right winger has tracked the first runner.
The left winger tracks last, once the switch brings a new runner on the left.

questions.q: Blue's left back now joins as the fourth runner. Which picture restores the numbers?
questions.explain: Yes. The winger tracks the extra runner, so each back keeps one forward and midfield stays central.
choiceExplanations: That empties the middle. The winger is the spare player who should track the outside runner.
Nobody tracks the new runner, so our left back must choose between two attackers.
Yes. The winger tracks the extra runner, so each back keeps one forward and midfield stays central.
